title: Splitting a Twelfth
statement: How many ordered pairs of positive integers $(x, y)$ satisfy $\dfrac1x + \dfrac1y = \dfrac1{12}$?
insight: Clear denominators and complete the product: xy − 12x − 12y = 0 becomes (x − 12)(y − 12) = 144, so solutions match divisors of 144.
redHerring: Bounding x and testing values one by one.
hints: Add a constant to both sides of $xy - 12x - 12y = 0$ so the left side factors.
$(x-12)(y-12) = 144$. Can the factors be negative? How many divisors does $144$ have?
solution: $12y + 12x = xy$, so $(x-12)(y-12) = 144$. Both $x, y > 12$ (since $\tfrac1x < \tfrac1{12}$), so both factors are positive. Ordered pairs correspond to positive divisors of $144 = 2^4\cdot3^2$: $(4+1)(2+1) = 15$.
